title: Gmail for founders on Mac: reply to investors and customers faster by voice
metaTitle: Gmail for founders on Mac: shortcuts, templates and limits
description: Gmail for founders on Mac: set up shortcuts and templates, know the sending limits, and let Lazur draft replies from the email on your screen.
intro: Gmail for founders on a Mac is mostly about replies to investors, customers and hires. Gmail runs in your browser, so most of the speed comes from settings, templates and shortcuts. This page covers those settings first, then the sending limits, then where Lazur fits.
tldr: Gmail runs in your browser on a Mac. A January 2026 third-party guide says Google has no Gmail app for macOS.
Keyboard shortcuts and templates are both off until you turn them on in Settings.
A personal Gmail account can be blocked from sending for 1 to 24 hours after more than 500 emails in a day.
Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask Lazur where a button is, or to draft a reply you read before you send.

blocks.text: Gmail for founders on a Mac runs in the browser

Most founders on a Mac use Gmail in a browser tab. Google does not appear to offer a Gmail app for macOS. A third-party guide updated on January 12, 2026 says the same thing. That guide comes from Mailmeteor, not Google, so check Google's help pages before you rely on it.

You have three practical choices. You can keep Gmail in its own Chrome or Edge window, which looks and feels like an app. You can also try a paid Mac client such as Mimestream. Mailmeteor lists Mimestream as macOS only, with a 14-day trial. Check Mimestream's own site for current prices.

Whichever way you go, the speed comes from Gmail itself. Settings, shortcuts and templates do most of the work. The rest of this page takes them in order of payoff, starting with the one that costs nothing.
Turn on Gmail keyboard shortcuts on Mac before anything else

Gmail keyboard shortcuts are off until you switch them on. Open Settings > See all settings from the gear icon. Find the Keyboard shortcuts section, choose Keyboard shortcuts on, then click Save Changes at the bottom of the page.
On a Mac, press Command where Windows users press Ctrl. Press Shift + / at any time to open Gmail's shortcut list. That list is the real reference, so keep it open during your first week.

items: c: start a new message.
e: archive the open conversation. Google's list also gives ] and [.
/: jump to the search box.
⌘ Return: send the message you are writing.
⌘ ;: jump to the next misspelled word. Google says this one works only on Mac.

blocks.title: Off until you turn them on
blocks.text: Shortcuts must be turned on in Settings. Until then, pressing e does nothing. Check the setting first if a shortcut seems broken.

Shortcuts pay off in a triage session. You open the inbox, read the top message, press e to archive it, and move on. Messages that used to take a minute each can take far less. Time one session before and after, so you know the gain is real.
Gmail templates for the replies you send every week
Founders write the same few emails again and again. A warm intro reply. A pricing note. A request for a deck. Gmail calls these templates, and older guides call them canned responses.

Templates work only from Gmail on a computer, not the phone app. They are also off by default. To turn them on, go to Settings > See all settings > Advanced. Click Enable next to Templates, then click Save Changes.
Save a template in four steps

items: Click Compose and write the email once, the way you want to send it again.
Click More options at the bottom of the compose window.
Choose Templates > Save draft as template > Save as new template.
Give it a name you will recognize, such as Investor intro reply.

blocks.text: To insert a template later, open a new message and choose More options > Templates. Pick the template, then read it before you send. Change the name, the day and any number. A reply that says Tuesday on a Thursday looks careless.

Two rules keep templates safe. First, you can overwrite a template with Save draft as template > Overwrite Template. Second, deleting a template is permanent and cannot be recovered. Check the name and text before you delete anything.

Here is a worked example. You meet a potential investor on Monday. By Wednesday you have sent three similar replies: a thanks, a deck request, and a meeting offer. Save each one as a template. Next time, insert it, change the first name, and send. You save the typing and keep the wording consistent.
Send a template automatically with a Gmail filter

A filter can send a template as a reply. Google's help page says to create a filter and select Send template in it. Use this for narrow matches only, such as one signup form or one subject line that your tool always uses.

Broad filters cause trouble. A filter that matches the word pricing could answer a journalist, a co-founder or a customer who wanted a human. Test the filter with one sender first. Widen it only after the reply looks right every time.
The steps for building the filter itself are in [how to create a filter in Gmail on Mac](/how-to/create-a-filter-in-gmail).
Gmail sending limits to know before launch day

Gmail limits how much you can send. A personal account can be blocked after more than 500 emails in a day. It can also be blocked after a single message to more than 500 total recipients. When that happens, you can usually send again within 1 to 24 hours.

rows: 2,000 total across To, Cc and Bcc, with up to 500 external
No sending for up to 24 hours, receiving still works
blocks.caption: Sending limits from Google's Gmail Help and Workspace Admin Help pages.

blocks.text: Workspace accounts have much higher numbers. Google's admin help says a standard account can send 2,000 messages per user per rolling 24 hours. If you exceed a limit, you cannot send for up to 24 hours. Mail still comes in.

Here is a worked example. You want to tell 800 customers about a price change. As one message, that is more than 500 total recipients on a personal account. Split the list into two sends of 400 each. Count the recipients in To, Cc and Bcc before you press send.

The common mistake is putting the whole list in Bcc. Bcc still counts toward the total. For a true bulk send, use a mail merge or a dedicated tool. Lazur drafts the text, but it does not send mail for you in bulk.
Attachments and the Gmail 25 MB limit

Personal Gmail accounts cap attachments at 25 MB, according to Google's help page on attaching files. A pitch deck with embedded video can pass that fast. Check the file size before you start the reply, not after you have typed three paragraphs.
When a file is too big, send a link. Put the file in a shared folder and paste the link into the email. Check the sharing setting first, so the investor can open the file without asking for access.

Two how-to pages cover the steps. Use [how to attach a file in Gmail on Mac](/how-to/attach-a-file-in-gmail) for the attach steps. Use [how to search emails with attachments in Gmail on Mac](/how-to/search-emails-with-attachments-in-gmail) to find the deck you sent last month.
Apple Mail as a Gmail alternative on Mac, and the Workspace sign-in catch

Apple Mail is the main native alternative on a Mac. Apple Mail 9.3 or later can add a Google account with the Google provider. That sign-in uses OAuth, so you approve access in a Google sign-in window.

Workspace accounts changed on May 1, 2025. Since that date, Workspace accounts no longer accept a username and password alone from third-party apps. If your company runs Workspace, expect the Google sign-in step. Ask your admin if the sign-in fails.

Choose Apple Mail if you want mail in a native app and you can handle the sign-in step. Stay in the browser if you want fewer moving parts. Either way, the sending limits in the section above still apply.
Gmail Offline for flights and bad Wi-Fi

Gmail Offline lets you read and reply without a connection. It works only in Google Chrome. It does not work in Incognito or guest profiles. Chrome must stay open for messages to sync, and the setup works with one account.
Set it up before you travel, while the connection is good. Open Chrome once before you leave so the mail syncs. Then your inbox is there when the signal drops.
What the time survey says about founders and email

A 2016 Business Pulse survey from The Alternative Board found email was the top time drain for 33% of entrepreneurs. The same release reports that owners spend 32% of their time on email and web browsing. The sample size is not stated, so treat these as a rough signal.

The survey measures how strained people feel, not how many hours they spend. Measure your own week instead. Count the replies you send and note how long each one takes. Then pick the one template or filter that removes the most of them.
Where Lazur fits in your Gmail routine

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on screen, and Lazur answers out loud. In Gmail, that covers questions about the email, where a button sits, and how to turn on a setting you have not used before.

Ask where something is and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it on your screen. Ask how to do something and Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click. Lazur does not click for you. You stay in control of Gmail the whole time.
A reply in one breath

items: Open the thread and click Reply.
Hold ⌥ ⌘ and say: reply, thanks for the intro, happy to talk next week.
Read the draft in the compose box. Change the name and the day.
Click Send yourself. Lazur never sends for you.

blocks.text: For longer text, hold fn to dictate. Dictation writes clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. You also get snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots. Dictation is unlimited on both Lazur plans.

Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so Lazur can answer. They are not stored, and content is never used to train AI models. Plans and the trial are on [the pricing page](/pricing).
Mistakes founders make in Gmail

items: Leaving shortcuts off and clicking through every message by hand.
Building templates on the phone. Templates work only on a computer.
Using a broad filter that auto-replies to everyone who writes in.
Sending one message to a whole customer list over the limit.
Attaching a deck over 25 MB to a personal account.
Deleting a template and expecting to get it back. Deletion is permanent.
Typing a Workspace password into Apple Mail again and again.

blocks.text: Most of these come from skipping one setting or one warning. Read the list once, then check your own habits against it.
What to do next this week

items: Turn on keyboard shortcuts and templates today.
Save your three most common replies as templates.
Find your account type in the limits table, then plan any big send around it.
Try Lazur on your Mac. Start on the download page, and check plans on the pricing page.

blocks.text: Lazur runs on the Mac, on Apple silicon and Intel. Windows is planned, not available. The Pro trial needs no credit card. [Download Lazur](/download) when you are ready.

faq.question: Is there an official Gmail app for Mac?
faq.answer: Not that we could confirm. A January 2026 third-party guide says Google has no Gmail desktop app for Mac. Use Gmail in a browser window or try a paid Mac client. Check Google's help pages for updates.

faq.question: Can I use Gmail templates on my phone?
faq.answer: No. Google's help page says templates can be turned on and used only from Gmail on a computer, not the phone app.

faq.question: Will Lazur read my whole inbox?
faq.answer: No. Lazur sees the screen and listens only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you, and they are not stored.

faq.question: Can Lazur send emails for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur drafts and types text, and it guides you one click at a time. It does not click buttons or send mail. You read the draft and press Send yourself.

faq.question: How many emails can I send in a day?
faq.answer: On a personal account, Gmail can block sending after more than 500 emails in one day. On Google Workspace, the standard limit is 2,000 messages per user per rolling 24 hours. Limits can change, so check Google's pages for your account.

faq.question: Why does Apple Mail reject my Workspace password?
faq.answer: Since May 1, 2025, Google Workspace accounts no longer accept a username and password alone from third-party apps. Use the Google sign-in step that Apple Mail opens, or ask your admin.

faq.question: Does Gmail Offline work in Safari?
faq.answer: No. Gmail Offline works only in Google Chrome, not in Incognito or guest profiles. Chrome must stay open for messages to sync.
